question.worked_solution:
The "square of a difference" formula states that

$$
{t}^{2}-2at+{a}^{2}=(t-a)^{2}.
$$

We will use this formula to factor the given trinomial. Our trinomial is

$$
{t}^{2}-22t+121.
$$

First, we write the constant term as a perfect square:

$$
\begin{aligned}{t}^{2}-22t+{11}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we factor a $2$ out of the linear term:

$$
\begin{aligned}{t}^{2}-2\cdot 11t+{11}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we factor the trinomial using the square of difference formula with $a=11.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}(t-11)^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
